<user>
Return the next passage of fiction.

I take a short break in the common room. If Seraphel is there and not occupied in a conversation, I ask, "What do you like reading for pleasure?" Otherwise I sit with my book.
</user>

item.text:
You mark your place and carry the blue volume into the common room.

The card game has spread across most of the low table. Coins, sugared nuts, and a brass collar stud now form the stakes. Dena is winning. Rashid has removed his immaculate coat and draped it safely beyond the reach of spilled wine, while Thessaly studies every card as though preparing an appeal.

Seraphel sits apart from them in a leather chair near the fireplace. Caelindra has gone upstairs, and no one is speaking to her. Firelight passes through the edges of her small white wings.

You take the neighboring chair and set the Council book across your knees.

“What do you like reading for pleasure?”

Seraphel looks from the dry blue volume to you.

“Bad travel accounts, full of weather and cost;  
The best are the ones where the writer gets lost.

“And poems read out, so their rhythms are known;  
What do you read when the choice is your own?”
